newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: The Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Victor loading 54,652 tonnes soybeans. Flag Zannis loading 33,500 tonnes soymeal. Syn Pulko loading 26,500 tonnes soymeal. Solidarnosc loading 56,250 tonnes soybeans/meal. Waiting to dock, four vessels to load soybeans, three to load soymeal and one for mixed cargo.
Road: 1,277 trucks carrying soybeans arrived between July 4 and 6, as well as 601 trucks with soymeal and 157 trucks with vegetable oils including soyoil.

Loading: In June, the port loaded a total of 429,076 tonnes soybeans, up from 180,552 tonnes in June 1996. In addition, it loaded 732,977 tonnes soymeal, up from 590,051 last year, and 134,186 tonnes soyoil, compared with none the previous year. Stocks: no figures available.
Vessels: At public terminal, Huta Sendzimira loading 30,000 tonnes soybeans. No vessels waiting to dock. At Cargill private terminal, no vessels docked or waiting to dock.
Road: 14 trucks carrying 374 tonnes soymeal arrived on July 6.
